answer.generated: The exploration parameter ε controls the probability of choosing a random action during each step, balancing exploration (learning new information) against exploitation (using known good actions). By setting ε appropriately, the algorithm can gather more diverse experience early on, improving its Q-function estimates, while still leveraging known high-reward actions as it gains confidence. This parameterization allows Q-learning to adaptively explore the state-action space without requiring explicit guidance, enabling effective learning in environments where optimal policies are unknown.
